newsitem.title: USA: Edison Calif. nuke may shut for inspection next yr.
newsitem.headline: Edison Calif. nuke may shut for inspection next yr.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co may shut a 1,087 megawatt (MW) unit at the San Onofre nuclear plant for a short-term inspection sometime next spring, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday.

Such an outage is one of the options being explored following the discovery of erosion of heat transfer tubing in San Onofre's unit 3 during its current refueling outage, NRC spokesman Breck Henderson said.
"They are considering a mid-cycle outage to inspect the steam generators," as part of an agreement with the NRC to allow the unit to restart later this month, he noted.
Nuclear plants typically shut for refueling every 18 months or so.
If it goes forward, the outage would be as brief as possible, probably lasting two weeks, and would take place between next April and June, Henderson said.
The unit, which has been shut for refueling since April, is expected to restart around June 26, but final approval from the NRC is still needed.
The agency will meet Wednesday with Edison to review the latest technical data and expects to make a final decision before the unit's scheduled restart, Henderson said.
Officals at Edison, the plant's operator and 75-percent owner, could not be immediately reached for comment.
